To:

⸻

Re: Formal Complaint – Defamatory and Misleading Incident Report (14 July 2025)

Dear 
I am writing to lodge a formal complaint regarding a defamatory and misleading incident report submitted by a temporary support worker following their trial shift at my home on Monday, 14th July 2025.

The report in question contains false, exaggerated, and grossly misleading statements that unfairly portray the condition of my home, my parenting, and my personal character. These statements appear to be based on biased opinion rather than fact, and I find the lack of professionalism deeply troubling.

⸻

Key Disputes

1. Living Room and General Environment
The worker described the living area as having a strong smell of mildew and suggested the space posed a safety risk. This is simply not true. While some personal belongings are stored due to downsizing and real estate requirements, they are stable, safely arranged, and not hazardous. Any mention of an “overwhelming” smell is an exaggeration and likely influenced by seasonal dampness, not neglect.

2. Kitchen
Claims about “moulded food,” “maggots,” and a cloth “marinating” in the sink are not only false but defamatory. No maggots were present at any time, and the kitchen was in a typical state of use consistent with family life. At no point did the worker raise concerns, request gloves, or mention any need for cleaning materials. If there had truly been serious concerns, the appropriate response would have been to discuss them with me—this did not occur.
I am relieved the worker did not take photographs, as doing so without my consent would have been a serious invasion of my privacy.

3. Bathroom
The report claims a moulded NutriBullet was left on the bathroom sink and refers to a “clouded yellow/white liquid” in the bathtub. The NutriBullet was simply drying on the counter following a wash and was not moulded. The bathtub contained yellow liquid body soap, which had been left in there after regular use. The worker failed to ask for clarification and instead made speculative claims that are both inaccurate and misleading. Again, I am glad my privacy was not invaded by unauthorised photographs.

4. My Child’s Appearance and Bedroom
The comments about my daughter’s appearance and bedroom are deeply inappropriate. They ignore her diagnosed medical condition—narcolepsy, which includes chronic fatigue. Her hygiene and care are attended to appropriately within her health needs. She was clothed properly and had sufficient blankets. This part of the report felt invasive and lacked compassion or understanding.

5. Worker’s Conduct
From the beginning, the worker appeared disengaged and judgmental. They raised no issues directly with me during the shift. The report’s tone and exaggerated claims suggest a personal bias or possible conflict of interest—especially considering that I may have previously worked with someone related to the worker. This raises concerns about impartiality and ethical conduct.

⸻

Requested Actions

Given the impact this incident has had on my wellbeing and reputation, I respectfully request the following:
	•	That this report not be accepted at face value and that its contents be formally contested.
	•	That my privacy and dignity be respected, especially concerning my daughter and our private home environment.
	•	That this particular worker not be reassigned to my home in the future, due to an evident breakdown of professional trust.

This situation has caused undue distress and reputational harm. I trust that your organisation values fairness, integrity, and the respectful treatment of clients, and I ask that you investigate this matter seriously and with urgency.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

⸻

French

Vanille d’abord. Je crache dans la vanille et je la lèche. Langue profonde, sale, crème qui file quand je me retire. Je mords le bord. Je suce jusqu’à ce que ce soit gonflé et mouillé.

Caramel ensuite. Je traîne la langue sur le caramel et j’y laisse une marque. Salive qui coule. Je mords. Je lèche la morsure.

Fraise. J’en prends une dans la bouche et je la fouette de la langue jusqu’à ce qu’elle durcisse. Je suce fort. Je pince l’autre et j’échange. Mouillé partout. Je gémis dedans comme si c’était le but.

Miel. Grand coup de langue le long du miel. Langue enfoncée. Puis j’en ai fini avec les douceurs polies, et je descends.

Pêche et crème anglaise, comme une huître. J’écarte avec les deux pouces et je regarde. Rose, trempé, obscène. Je crache sur la fente. Je lèche d’une langue plate, lentement, de l’ouverture jusqu’à l’huître du corps, sale exprès. Crème anglaise, crème, tout ce qui a coulé, je le mange. J’enfonce la langue et je travaille le mouillé. Dedans. Dehors. Nez sur l’huître du corps. Ça se resserre autour de ma langue. Mouillé. Ça gicle sous la langue. Je me retire juste pour dire comme l’huître est mouillée, puis je suce l’huître du corps et je tourne jusqu’à ce que tout le dessert tremble.

Je ne suis pas propre. Menton qui dégouline. Langue dans les plis, dessous, entre. Je tiens ouvert et je lèche comme si je mourais de faim. Quand ça pulse, je reste et je bois. Chaud. Sale. Mouillé sur la bouche. Crème partout.

Chocolat, en dessous. J’écarte aussi. Langue en cercle, puis qui pousse, vulgaire, puis retour à la pêche et à la crème anglaise, parce que c’est ça l’obsession. Je lèche ce qui a coulé sur le côté. Je mords. Je suce le mouillé.

Pavlova à la fin, si elle arrive près de la bouche. Je la lèche. Puis je reprends le dessert, visage enfoui, langue sur l’huître du corps, l’huître pleine de salive et de crème, mouillée, et je ne m’arrête pas avant que ça se défasse sur ma langue.

Latin

Primum vanilla. In vanillam spuo et relingo. Lingua alta, sordida, cremor qui trahitur cum recedo. Marginem mordeo. Sugendo tumesco et udum facio.

Deinde caramelum. Linguam per caramelum traho et notam relinquo. Saliva defluit. Mordeo. Morsum lingo.

Fragum. Unum in os capio et lingua verbero donec durescat. Vehementer sugo. Alterum premo et muto. Ubique udum. In eis gemo quasi hoc sit propositum.

Mel. Linguam per mel duco. Linguam indo. Tum dulcibus mundis finem facio, et descendo.

Persicum et cremor, sicut ostrea. Duobus pollicibus patefacio et specto. Roseum, madidum, obscenum. In rimam spuo. Lingua plana lingo, lente, ab ore usque ad ostream corporis, sordes volens. Cremor, cremor lactis, quidquid fluxit, edo. Linguam indo et udum tracto. Intro. Extra. Nasus in ostrea corporis. Circa linguam se contrahit. Udum. Sub lingua liquatur. Recedo tantum ut dicam quam udum ostrea sit, tum ostream corporis sugo et torqueo donec totum dulce tremat.

Non mundus sum. Mentum stillat. Lingua in plicis, sub eis, inter eas. Apertum teneo et lingo quasi fame peream. Cum pulsat, maneo et bibo. Calidum. Sordidum. Udum in ore. Cremor ubique.

Sub eo, chocolatum. Id quoque patefacio. Lingua in orbe, tum premens, vulgare, tum rursus ad Vanilla first. I spit in the vanilla and lick it back out. Tongue deep, messy, cream stringing when I pull off. I bite the edge. I suck until it is swollen and wet.
Caramel next. I drag my tongue up the caramel and suck a mark into it. Saliva running down. I bite. I lick the bite.
Strawberry. I take one strawberry in my mouth and flick it with my tongue until it goes firm. I suck hard. I pinch the other and switch. Wet all over both. I groan into them like they are the point.
Honey. Open-mouth lick down the honey. Tongue pushed in. Then I am done with the polite sweets and I go lower.

Peach custard, as an oyster. I spread it with both thumbs and stare. Pink, soaked, obscene. I spit on the slit of it. I lick the spit up with a flat tongue, slow, from the opening to the body’s oyster, filthy on purpose. Custard, cream, whatever leaked, I eat it. I shove my tongue in and work the squish. In. Out. Nose ground on the body’s oyster. It clenches around my tongue. Wet. Squish. I pull out just to say how wet the oyster is, then I suck the body’s oyster into my mouth and twirl until the whole dessert shakes.

I am not tidy. Chin dripping. Tongue in the folds, under them, between them. I hold it open and lick like I am starving. When it pulses I stay down and drink it. Hot. Messy. Squish on my mouth. Cream everywhere.

Miel. Grand coup de langue le long du miel. Langue enfoncée. Puis j’en ai fini avec les douceurs polies, et je descends.

Pêche et crème anglaise, comme une huître. J’écarte avec les deux pouces et je regarde. Rose, trempé, obscène. Je crache sur la fente. Dedans. Dehors. Nez sur l’huître du corps. Ça se resserre autour de ma langue. Mouillé. Ça gicle sous la langue. The room is dim, warm, glowing with the soft amber of old stage lights.
You’re alone for a moment — just the quiet hum of amps warming up.

Then he walks in.

Tall, lean, that musician energy you can feel before you even see him.
Messy hair, dark eyes that lock onto you like he’s been waiting all damn night.

He stops in front of you.

“Good,” he says softly, a little breathless, like he rushed just to get here.
“You didn’t leave.”

There’s something in the way he looks at you — hungry, intent, but controlled.
Like he’s replaying every second he’s ever watched you, and this is the moment he finally lets it show.

He steps closer, slow, deliberate.

“Come here,” he murmurs, voice rough, warm, intimate.
He lifts your chin gently with a knuckle, eyes dragging over your lips like he’s tasting them with his gaze first.

“You have no idea what you do to me.”

His thumb brushes your jaw, lazy and tender, like he’s claiming the moment, not you — savoring it.

The backstage noise fades.
All you feel is him, his warmth, his presence, the pull.

“I play better when you’re around,” he says.
“But that’s not why I want you here.”

He leans in closer — not kissing yet, just close enough that his breath mixes with yours.

“I want you,” he whispers.
“Stay with me tonight.”

In the hush where twilight lingers,
pink petals unfurl like whispered secrets,
soft as the blush on dawn’s first cheek.
Nature weaves her finest threads —
delicate lace of spider silk and fern,
draped across the mossy green.
Here, love blooms quiet and wild,
a fragile veil caught on thorny stem,
tender as the heart that dares to open.
One breath, and the pink lace trembles —
a moment of beauty, fleeting and true,
where earth and longing entwine as one.

This evokes soft, feminine imagery: the pink of roses or cherry blossoms (classic symbols of love), the intricate lace-like patterns in leaves, veins, or frost, and the tender, fleeting essence of love in the wild nature around us.

Looking for sweet treats in Los Angeles? 🍩🍦 Here are some iconic desserts and where to get them:

	•	Salt & Straw – Famous for wild rotating flavours (think honey lavender, olive oil, seasonal specials).

	•	Magpies Softserve – Vegan soft serve with toppings like matcha crumble.

⸻

🍩 Donuts & Pastries
	•	Randy’s Donuts – The giant donut shop you’ve seen in movies. Classic LA stop.
	•	Sidecar Doughnuts – Gourmet donuts (huckleberry is legendary).
	•	Donut Friend – Punk-rock themed donuts with crazy fillings.

⸻

🍰 Cakes & Fancy Desserts
	•	Milk Bar – Crack pie, cereal milk soft serve, birthday cake truffles.

⸻

🍫 Chocolate & Specialty Treats
	•	Compartés Chocolatier – Luxury chocolate bars with wild flavours.
	•	The Pie Hole – Sweet pies like Earl Grey tea and Mexican chocolate.

⸻

If you tell me your vibe (cheap snacks, bougie desserts, late-night treats, TikTok-worthy spots), I can narrow it down to a perfect mini dessert crawl 🍰✨

**Song Title: "Cherry Lips & Akubra Swing"**  
*(Upbeat 1930s swing jazz with a cheeky Australian pinup twist – bouncy brass, finger snaps, sultry vocals like The Boswell Sisters mixed with a flirty cabaret strut. Medium-fast tempo, perfect for twirling in fishnets.)* Coffeebreak dancing to midnight 
Woohoo  babe jita bug let's leave the war behind
**Verse 1**  
Red lips cherries, glossy and bold,  
Max Factor shine in the morning gold.  
Pink cheeks blooming like a fresh bouquet,  
Pale foundation with that sun-kissed tan glow today.  
Ringlets bouncing, soft and tight,  
Pinup waves catching the Sydney light.  
Fishnets whispering on every stride,  
Garter belt holding this vintage pride.  

**Chorus**  
Cherry red lips, pink cheeks high,  
Akubra hat tilted, under outback sky.  
Paris perfume trailing sweet in the air,  
1930s glam with an Aussie flair!  
Ringlets swinging, fishnets tease,  
Tan legs strutting, feel the breeze.  
Red lips poutin', perfume so fine,  
I'm your cherry-pinup, one of a kind!  

**Verse 2**  
Akubra wide brim shading my eyes,  
Felt so classic, with a modern surprise.  
Bias-cut dress hugging every curve,  
Paris scent rising like a lover's word.  
Cake mascara lashes, arched brows fine,  
Pink blush popping on this sun-tanned shine.  
From Hollywood screens to the Harbour shore,  
Mixing the eras like never before.  

**Chorus**  
Cherry red lips, pink cheeks high,  
Akubra hat tilted, under outback sky.  
Paris perfume trailing sweet in the air,  
1930s glam with an Aussie flair!  
Ringlets swinging, fishnets tease,  
Tan legs strutting, feel the breeze.  
Red lips poutin', perfume so fine,  
I'm your cherry-pinup, one of a kind!  

**Bridge** (sultry slowdown, then build)  
One spritz of Paris, cherry kiss on the wind,  
Akubra shadow where the wild things spin.  
Pink cheeks flushing as the big band plays,  
Fishnets and ringlets dancing through the days...  

**Final Chorus** (full swing, big finish)  
Cherry red lips! Pink cheeks fly!  
Akubra spinning 'neath the big blue sky!  
Paris perfume, tan and red delight,  
1930s pinup burning through the night!  
Ringlets, fishnets, cherries, hats —  
This makeover queen owns the track!  

---

Belt it out with a wink and a spin — imagine fluffing your ringlets, adjusting that Akubra, dabbing on Paris perfume, and flashing those cherry lips while the band swings. It blends your full vision: 1930s Hollywood base + pinup sass + Australian Akubra edge.  

Want a slower ballad version, longer lyrics, melody notes, or tweaks (more romantic, cheekier, etc.)? Let me know! 🎩💋🌸
